title: helios run prints a traceback for a bad workflow.toml instead of a refusal
description:
Found while reviewing hel-xm0. src/helios/commands/run.py calls config_mod.load(hub) outside any exception handler, and src/helios/cli.py main() wraps nothing: it calls the command function and returns its value. So every configuration error reaches the user of helios run as a Python traceback with exit 1.

SPEC section 2.3 requires the opposite: a configuration error prints helios: <message> to stderr and exits 2, naming the dotted key. Other command modules already handle this; helios run does not.

This became visible with the new telemetry block, whose refusal helios: telemetry.enabled requires telemetry.endpoint is user-facing by design and is currently unreachable in that form through helios run. It is not caused by that work: any unknown key or wrong type in workflow.toml has always produced a traceback here.

Check the other command modules while fixing this, since the same omission may exist elsewhere, and prefer one shared handler over a copy in each module.
acceptance_criteria: helios run against a hub whose .agents/workflow.toml has an unknown key, a value of the wrong type, or telemetry.enabled true with an empty telemetry.endpoint prints exactly helios: <message> to stderr, naming the dotted key where section 2.3 requires it, and exits 2 with no traceback. A test covers each of those three cases through the command entry point, not by calling config.load directly. Every other command module that loads configuration is checked and covered the same way.

title: Export OpenTelemetry spans to Langfuse over OTLP
description:
Decision K, SPEC section 18, closed 2026-09-16. helios emits no telemetry today. SPEC batch 12 writes a new section 21 stating the rules; this bead makes the code match them. Do not start until those rules are on main.

Shape. A new module src/helios/telemetry.py builds OpenTelemetry spans and exports them over OTLP/HTTP using opentelemetry-sdk and the OTLP HTTP exporter. The Langfuse SDK is not a dependency, so any OTLP backend works and the backend can be changed without changing helios. These facts were confirmed against Langfuse documentation on 2026-09-16 and must not be re-researched: OTLP over HTTP with protobuf or JSON, no gRPC, signal specific path /api/public/otel/v1/traces, headers Authorization Basic of base64 of public key colon secret key plus x-langfuse-ingestion-version 4, self hosting from v3.22.0. Langfuse's legacy ingestion API is sunset on 2026-11-16, so build on the OpenTelemetry endpoint only.

Configuration is a new [telemetry] block with enabled defaulting to false, endpoint, timeout_s defaulting to 5 and service_name defaulting to helios. Credentials come from the environment variables LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY and LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY only, never from workflow.toml, because that file is committed.

The rule that matters most: export never fails a run. It is bounded by timeout_s, every exporter exception is caught, no exit code changes, and a failed or skipped export is recorded once on the attempt record as a note. An unreachable, slow or misconfigured backend must leave helios run and helios merge behaving exactly as they do with telemetry disabled. The attempt record under project.runs stays the source of truth and helios never reads telemetry back.

Spans carry identifiers, enumerated statuses, timings, commit hashes and check names only. They never carry prompt text, report text, agent output, file paths, or anything matched by project.confidential.

Read SPEC sections 5, 21, 7.1 and 12 before writing code. The SPEC is the contract; where this description and the SPEC differ, the SPEC wins.
acceptance_criteria: Every rule of SPEC section 21 holds in code, each with a test asserting exact values. A fake OTLP receiver on localhost receives the attempt trace and the merge trace and the tests assert the span names, the parent and child structure, the attribute keys and the two required headers. With telemetry.enabled false no network call is made at all. With an unreachable endpoint, helios run and helios merge finish with the same exit codes and the same stdout as with telemetry disabled, within timeout_s, and the attempt record carries exactly one note naming the reason. telemetry.enabled true with an empty endpoint is refused naming both keys. A missing or empty credential variable exports nothing and is not a refusal. No span carries prompt text, report text, agent output or a file path. The full suite stays green and pyright reports 0 errors on every changed file.
close_reason: Merged to main at 0a5d448. New src/helios/telemetry.py is the only module importing OpenTelemetry; the rest of helios builds a plain Span tree and calls export. Export runs in a daemon thread joined with timeout_s and checks SpanExportResult directly, because BatchSpanProcessor.force_flush reports success even when the exporter failed. Attempt and merge traces wired into run.py and merge.py, only phases that ran get a span. Credentials env-only. OTel packages are a telemetry extra, not core dependencies, matching the claims precedent; imports stay lazy so a missing extra yields a note, not a failed run. Suite 1264 passing. Follow-ups filed: hel-5eh for two SPEC section 21 gaps, hel-f1g for the config traceback in helios run.

title: Replace project.test and project.typecheck with an ordered list of named checks
description:
Decision B, SPEC section 18, closed 2026-09-16. Today a project gets exactly two check strings, project.test and project.typecheck, so a repository needing two test runners or a lint step separate from a typecheck cannot express that. SPEC batch 12 writes the replacement rules; this bead makes the code match them. Do not start until those rules are on main.

The new shape is an array of tables, [[project.check]], each with name, command and an optional when of run, merge or both, default both. The order of the entries is the order the checks run, which is why it is an array and not a table keyed by name. project.test and project.typecheck become sugar for exactly two entries, name test with when merge and name typecheck with when both, which reproduces today's behaviour exactly. Setting either old key together with any [[project.check]] entry is a refusal naming both keys.

Code anchors. ProjectConfig is src/helios/config.py:77, with test and typecheck as plain str fields and a validation table above it. The run performs its checks in src/helios/run.py around lines 1000 to 1050, where the bead test and the typecheck each build an envelope Check and call _run_shell. The merge reruns them in src/helios/merge.py:523, which loops over a two element tuple of name and command. envelope.Check at src/helios/envelope.py:183 already carries an arbitrary name, command, exit_code, detail and log_path, so it needs no change.

Read SPEC sections 5, 7.1 step 9, 12 step 4 and 4.3 before writing code. The SPEC is the contract; where this description and the SPEC differ, the SPEC wins.

title: SPEC section 21: the merge export has no note target and the child order contradicts the run steps
description:
Two gaps found while reviewing hel-xm0, both in SPEC section 21.

First, the note rule has no target for a merge. Section 21 says a failed or skipped export is recorded once on the attempt record as a note naming the reason. A merge has no attempt record, so the implementation discards the return value of telemetry.export for the merge trace and a failed merge export is silent. Decide what a merge should do and state it. The cheapest correct answer is probably to say plainly that a failed merge export is silent, because helios merge has a strict output contract, every stderr line prefixed helios: with fixed exit codes, and the bead comment markers follow the replay rule of section 7.5, so neither is a good place to put a telemetry note. Whatever is decided, section 21 must say it rather than leave it to the reader.

Second, the listed child order contradicts the real order. Section 21 lists the attempt children as launch, check.<name>, validate, commit. The run steps of section 7.1 put parse and classify, which is what the validate span covers, at step 8, before the checks at step 9 and the commit at step 10. The implementation emits the children in the order section 21 lists while giving each span its real timestamps, so the emitted order contradicts the timestamps it carries. Fix section 21 to list launch, validate, check.<name>, commit, then make the code match.

Section 21 lists the attempt children in the order they actually occur, launch then validate then check.<name> then commit, and src/helios/run.py builds them in that order, with a test asserting the emitted child order matches the order of their timestamps.

2026-09-15 lesson (hel-oj1 rounds 4 to 7): proving a worktree HEAD is the verified commit rebased. No diff comparison works. git patch-id --stable strips whitespace; --verbatim ignores bytes after a NUL and mode lines; git show output bends to git config (diff.submodule=log splits the patch, ignoreSubmodules=all hides pointer changes). Final rule: cursor starts at merge-base(HEAD, main); for each commit c of output_base..output_commit run git merge-tree --write-tree --merge-base=<c^> <cursor> <c>, exit 1 refuses, then cursor = commit-tree of the replayed tree; the final cursor tree must equal HEAD's tree. A missing or empty merge-base refuses (exit 2), and every git call takes --no-replace-objects. Probes: tmp/fp-probe, tmp/replay-probe, tmp/seq-probe. But once the session is isolated by EnterWorktree, every git command is refused too, including read-only ones such as git status, because the rtk rewrite hides which git runs and the worktree guard will not allow a git it cannot attribute. Those two rules together mean neither the hub nor an isolated session can both edit and commit.

The pattern that works, in this order: create the worktree from the hub with plain git, git worktree add .claude/worktrees/<id> -b worktree-<id> followed by git worktree lock --reason keep; call EnterWorktree with the path, never with a name; make every edit; call ExitWorktree with action keep, which returns the session to the hub and leaves the branch and directory intact; then commit and merge from the hub, where git works normally. Writing the commit message to a file outside the repository and using git commit -F avoids quoting problems with multi-line messages.

This cost six refused edits and four refused git calls before it was understood. Subagents are unaffected: they never call EnterWorktree, so they edit and commit inside their worktree normally.
